shortlist.name: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — one of the world's largest users of external managers; runs dedicated external Asian-equity and hedge-fund mandates
shortlist.angle: ADIA outsources the majority of its book to external managers and has long-standing Asian-equity and hedge-fund programmes; the Abu Dhabi / Lunate network gives us a credible warm introduction that cold outreach could never buy, and ADIA is deliberately increasing Asia exposure.
shortlist.access: Warm intro through the Abu Dhabi network into ADIA's external-equities / Asia-Pacific desk (not a cold RFP).
shortlist.watchout: Very high operational-DD bar and a preference for managers with real capacity; unlikely to be a day-one seed.

shortlist.name: Mubadala Investment Company
shortlist.invests: Yes — external funds alongside direct; expanding manager relationships in Asia
shortlist.angle: Mubadala has been building out Asia (offices and China/Asia allocations) and backs external managers who can source regional alpha; the same Abu Dhabi network reaches it warmly.
shortlist.access: Abu Dhabi network into Mubadala's public-markets / Asia team.
shortlist.watchout: More direct/strategic than ADIA on the margin; frame us as an alpha source, not a co-investor.

shortlist.name: Sanabil Investments (PIF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — explicitly a fund investor; commits ~US$3bn+/yr to external managers and backs first-time / emerging funds
shortlist.angle: Sanabil is PIF's dedicated external-manager arm and one of the few sovereigns that systematically backs emerging and first-time managers — precisely our profile — with a stated appetite to diversify Saudi capital internationally.
shortlist.access: Sanabil external-managers team; a Gulf-network intro materially improves reception.
shortlist.watchout: Process is selective and Saudi-strategy aware; a China-only pitch may need an Asia/global framing.

shortlist.name: Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — heavy, long-standing external-manager user (via the Kuwait Investment Office, London)
shortlist.angle: One of the oldest sovereigns and a core external-manager allocator with a genuinely long horizon; the Gulf network provides a warm path, and KIA has historically supported differentiated managers.
shortlist.access: Kuwait Investment Office (London) external-equities / alternatives desks.
shortlist.watchout: Conservative, relationship-driven and slow; expect a multi-touch cultivation.

shortlist.name: Qatar Investment Authority (QIA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external funds alongside direct; explicit Asia pivot
shortlist.angle: QIA has publicly prioritised Asia (China/India) and uses external managers; a Gulf-network introduction plus an Asia-alpha story lines up with its stated direction.
shortlist.access: QIA public-markets / Asia team via the Gulf network.
shortlist.watchout: Headline-sensitive and selective; large minimums.

shortlist.name: China Investment Corporation — CIC International
shortlist.invests: Yes — extensive external-manager book for public equities, hedge funds and multi-asset (offshore)
shortlist.angle: Your flagship warm relationship, and — unlike most Chinese institutions — CIC International genuinely runs USD external mandates and prizes differentiated China/Asia alpha from an on-the-ground manager. This is the single best door to walk through first.
shortlist.access: Warm relationship, routed to CIC International's public-equities / hedge-fund manager-selection desk.
shortlist.watchout: Large-ticket bias and formal RFP cadence; be ready to absorb size and show institutional operations.

shortlist.name: National Council for Social Security Fund (NSSF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — outsources ~2/3 of assets; has granted offshore USD equity/FI mandates to global managers since 2006
shortlist.angle: China's sovereign pension reserve is one of the few mainland allocators that awards genuine offshore USD mandates to external managers, and it values long-horizon, governance-strong partners for its China/Asia and global sleeves.
shortlist.access: NSSF's overseas-investment department; mandate cycles are periodic and highly selective.
shortlist.watchout: Prizes stability and track record over flair; not a fast or a first-fund decision.

shortlist.name: The Hong Kong Jockey Club (Charities Trust)
shortlist.invests: Yes — ~25% in alternatives including hedge funds, via external managers
shortlist.angle: A large, sophisticated local endowment-style pool that already runs an external hedge-fund and alternatives programme in USD, and is reachable on home turf — an ideal early institutional reference LP.
shortlist.access: HKJC investment office directly; local relationships shorten the path.
shortlist.watchout: Institutional-grade diligence despite being local; not a rubber stamp.

shortlist.name: VMS Group
shortlist.invests: Yes — purpose-built to seed and accelerate managers, including public-equities long/short
shortlist.angle: A Cheng-family-backed HK seeder explicitly building a long/short equity platform — it exists to provide anchor capital and infrastructure to managers like us, on home turf and in USD.
shortlist.access: VMS's seeding / acceleration team directly.
shortlist.watchout: Primarily relevant if the vehicle is long/short; economics (revenue share / equity) come attached.

shortlist.name: Sun Hung Kai & Co. Limited (SHK Capital Partners)
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates to external hedge funds via its multi-manager platform, and can anchor with principal capital
shortlist.angle: A listed HK investment firm that both allocates to external managers and deploys balance-sheet capital to anchor them — a rare local source of day-one, USD anchor money. (Distinct from Sun Hung Kai Properties, the developer.)
shortlist.access: SHK Capital Partners / the multi-manager team, locally.
shortlist.watchout: Cheque sizes are meaningful but not sovereign-scale; alignment on terms matters.

shortlist.name: HKMA Exchange Fund — Long-Term Growth Portfolio
shortlist.invests: Yes — the LTGP allocates to external managers (though tilted to private markets)
shortlist.angle: The home regulator's investment arm, whose Long-Term Growth Portfolio backs external managers; being HK-based and known locally is a genuine advantage, even if the LTGP skews to private markets.
shortlist.access: HKMA / LTGP — institutional, and helped by local standing.
shortlist.watchout: Public-equities appetite is smaller than its private-markets book; large-institution process.

shortlist.name: Nan Fung Group / NF Trinity
shortlist.invests: Yes — documented external-manager programme that backs promising newer managers
shortlist.angle: A major HK family office with a real, documented programme of backing external and emerging managers in public markets — a warm, local, USD-capable early backer.
shortlist.access: NF Trinity's investment team; local family-office network.
shortlist.watchout: Discreet and relationship-led; sizing varies.

shortlist.name: Carret Private Capital
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client capital to external funds
shortlist.angle: A HK multi-family office with a value-investing orientation that allocates to external managers in USD — a natural fit if our process is fundamental and research-driven.
shortlist.access: Carret's investment / manager-selection team, locally.
shortlist.watchout: Cheques are FO-scale; needs a clear fit with their house style.

shortlist.name: Raffles Family Office
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client capital to external funds across Asia
shortlist.angle: One of Asia's larger multi-family offices (HK/Singapore), actively allocating client USD capital into external funds — a scalable channel to Asian family-office money.
shortlist.access: RFO's investment office; HK and Singapore desks.
shortlist.watchout: Gatekept by their fund-selection process; sizing per underlying family.

shortlist.name: AIA Group
shortlist.invests: Selective — uses external managers to complement in-house across pan-Asia
shortlist.angle: A HK-headquartered pan-Asian insurer that selectively hires external managers and understands the region; a differentiated Asia strategy can complement its in-house books.
shortlist.access: AIA Investment Management; frame around diversifying, liability-aware Asia exposure.
shortlist.watchout: Largely in-house; external mandates are selective and benchmark-aware.

shortlist.name: GIC
shortlist.invests: Yes — very large external-manager programme incl. Asian/EM equities and hedge funds
shortlist.angle: GIC is a core, permanent user of external managers and specifically hunts differentiated Asia and emerging-market alpha; a credible, research-driven Asia manager is squarely in its wheelhouse.
shortlist.access: GIC's External Managers Department (public equities / hedge funds).
shortlist.watchout: Rigorous, multi-year diligence and a capacity preference; rarely a first-fund seed.

shortlist.name: Temasek — Seviora (Fullerton / SeaTown)
shortlist.invests: Selective — mostly direct, but its Seviora asset-management arm (Fullerton, SeaTown) can allocate / co-invest
shortlist.angle: Temasek itself is direct-heavy, but its Seviora managers (Fullerton, SeaTown) are a more realistic route for external or co-investment capital tied to Asia.
shortlist.access: Seviora / SeaTown, rather than Temasek's direct-investing teams.
shortlist.watchout: Temasek proper rarely acts as a fund LP; keep expectations on the asset-management arm.

shortlist.name: National Pension Service (NPS)
shortlist.invests: Yes — large overseas external-manager and hedge-fund programmes via RFP
shortlist.angle: The world's third-largest pension is an aggressive overseas allocator that routinely hires external managers for global/Asia equities and hedge funds via formal RFPs.
shortlist.access: NPS overseas-investment / hedge-fund RFPs, typically via consultants and Seoul roadshows.
shortlist.watchout: Track-record and AUM thresholds; a structured, competitive RFP rather than a relationship sale.

shortlist.name: Korea Investment Corporation (KIC)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers across equities and hedge funds
shortlist.angle: Korea's sovereign fund is a committed external-manager user with a global remit and an appetite for differentiated overseas alpha.
shortlist.access: KIC's external-management team; Seoul-based process.
shortlist.watchout: Institutional thresholds; competitive selection.

shortlist.name: Public Officials Benefit Association (POBA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — very active overseas allocator, known to back specialist and newer managers
shortlist.angle: POBA is nimble, overseas-hungry and unusually willing to back specialist / emerging managers — the best-fit Korean allocator for a manager still building scale.
shortlist.access: POBA's CIO office; often via placement agents / consultants and manager roadshows in Seoul.
shortlist.watchout: Cheques are meaningful but sized to a mid-size fund; competitive process.

shortlist.name: Korea Teachers' Pension / Korea Post
shortlist.invests: Yes — regular overseas external mandates via RFP
shortlist.angle: Second-tier Korean asset owners that consistently award overseas USD mandates to external managers and are more approachable than NPS for a mid-size manager.
shortlist.access: Their overseas-investment teams via RFP / placement agents.
shortlist.watchout: Smaller tickets; RFP-driven and consultant-influenced.

shortlist.name: Pension Fund Association (PFA)
shortlist.invests: Yes — sophisticated user of external managers, including hedge funds and overseas equities
shortlist.angle: Japan's most sophisticated corporate-pension aggregator, genuinely open to overseas and alternative managers, and a reference name that pulls other Japanese pensions along.
shortlist.access: Usually intermediated by Japanese trust-bank gatekeepers / consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Slow, consensus-driven; near-always gatekeeper-gated.

shortlist.name: Japanese trust-bank gatekeepers (Sumitomo Mitsui Trust / MUFG Trust / Nomura EMP)
shortlist.invests: They select and package external managers for many underlying Japanese pension clients; Japan's Emerging Managers Programme explicitly welcomes foreign/newer managers
shortlist.angle: In Japan the gatekeeper is the market: one approval by a trust-bank platform or the government-backed Emerging Managers Programme unlocks capital from many underlying pensions at once — an efficient route for a foreign manager.
shortlist.access: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust / MUFG Trust manager-research desks; Nomura / SMBC EMP mandates.
shortlist.watchout: Long onboarding and Japanese-language / local-presence expectations.

shortlist.name: Japan Post Bank
shortlist.invests: Yes — large and growing alternatives book placed with external managers
shortlist.angle: A vast balance sheet running a fast-growing alternatives programme through external managers, actively diversifying overseas — real USD capital if accessed via the right gatekeeper.
shortlist.access: Via trust-bank gatekeepers / its alternatives team.
shortlist.watchout: Scale and process bias toward larger, established managers.

shortlist.name: Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers for global equities; expanding its manager pool
shortlist.angle: The world's largest pension uses external managers for global equities and has been widening its roster — the ultimate anchor, but a multi-year aspiration for a manager of our size.
shortlist.access: GPIF manager structure, via gatekeepers; extremely high bar.
shortlist.watchout: Scale and track-record thresholds make it aspirational, not first-wave.

shortlist.name: Future Fund
shortlist.invests: Yes — largely outsourced to external managers, including hedge funds and Asia
shortlist.angle: Australia's sovereign fund runs a near-fully-outsourced model and actively backs specialist external managers, with real hedge-fund and Asia appetite.
shortlist.access: Future Fund's external-manager teams (Melbourne).
shortlist.watchout: High bar; prefers managers with demonstrable edge and capacity.

shortlist.name: Hostplus
shortlist.invests: Yes — outsourced multi-manager, notably willing to back specialist / emerging managers (JANA-advised)
shortlist.angle: Among the Australian supers, Hostplus is the standout for backing specialist and emerging managers through an outsourced model — a rare institutional early-backer.
shortlist.access: Via its asset consultant JANA, and the Hostplus investment team.
shortlist.watchout: Consultant-gated (JANA rating is effectively the gate); AUD home bias.

shortlist.name: New Zealand Superannuation Fund
shortlist.invests: Yes — active external-manager programme, contrarian / opportunistic
shortlist.angle: A sophisticated, approachable sovereign fund with an active external-manager programme and a genuinely opportunistic, thesis-driven culture that engages with differentiated managers.
shortlist.access: Guardians of NZ Super's external-investments team (Auckland).
shortlist.watchout: Small team, high selectivity; wants a clear, articulable edge.

shortlist.name: Taiwan Bureau of Labor Funds (BLF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — regularly awards multi-year foreign (USD) equity mandates to external managers via public tender
shortlist.angle: BLF is one of Asia's most reliable sources of external mandates: it runs recurring public tenders for global and regional equity mandates in USD, awarded to external managers — a structured, repeatable entry point.
shortlist.access: BLF's public tender process, typically supported by global consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Tender criteria favour firm-level track record and AUM; fee-competitive.

shortlist.name: Employees Provident Fund (EPF)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external global mandates (incl. USD and Shariah) to external managers
shortlist.angle: A very large provident fund that outsources global equity mandates to external managers in USD and is diversifying beyond Malaysia — a real, if process-heavy, USD allocator.
shortlist.access: EPF's external-mandate / global-investment teams.
shortlist.watchout: Bureaucratic; some mandates carry Shariah or ESG constraints.

shortlist.name: Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (KWAP)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers for international equities
shortlist.angle: Malaysia's civil-service pension allocates internationally through external managers and is expanding overseas exposure, offering a mid-size USD mandate route.
shortlist.access: KWAP's international / external-manager desk.
shortlist.watchout: Smaller tickets; competitive and consultant-influenced.

shortlist.name: Pictet (Wealth / Asset Management)
shortlist.invests: Yes — open-architecture; places client and multi-manager capital into external funds
shortlist.angle: A Swiss open-architecture house that channels substantial client and multi-manager USD capital into external funds, with real Asia demand from its clients — and it can move faster than a pension.
shortlist.access: Pictet's manager-research / fund-selection and multi-manager desks.
shortlist.watchout: Needs a clear slot in their platform; wants operational robustness for client money.

shortlist.name: APG (ABP)
shortlist.invests: Yes — global external managers across EM/Asia equities and hedge funds
shortlist.angle: Europe's largest pension manager is a serious external allocator with dedicated EM/Asia equity and hedge-fund books and a genuine appetite for differentiated regional alpha.
shortlist.access: APG's manager-selection teams (Amsterdam / Hong Kong / New York).
shortlist.watchout: ESG-stringent and capacity-focused; institutional thresholds.

shortlist.name: Julius Baer
shortlist.invests: Yes — allocates client / advisory capital to external funds; strong Asia (HK/Singapore) presence
shortlist.angle: A pure-play private bank with a large Asian booking centre; it can aggregate HNW/family-office USD capital into a fund and its Asian clients actively want Asia strategies.
shortlist.access: Julius Baer's fund-research and Asia investment teams (Hong Kong / Singapore).
shortlist.watchout: Platform onboarding and suitability requirements; client-money DD.

shortlist.name: PGGM (PFZW)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers across public and alternative strategies
shortlist.angle: A large Dutch pension manager that allocates globally to external managers and is open to specialist regional strategies with a strong process and ESG alignment.
shortlist.access: PGGM's external-management team (Zeist).
shortlist.watchout: Strong ESG screen; longer diligence.

shortlist.name: Wellcome Trust
shortlist.invests: Yes — endowment model, backs external managers globally incl. Asia
shortlist.angle: One of the world's largest endowments, run on a Yale-style model that backs high-conviction external managers globally — and it has genuine appetite for differentiated Asia exposure.
shortlist.access: Wellcome's investment team directly (London); endowment-network references help.
shortlist.watchout: Highly selective, concentrated roster; wants exceptional, differentiated managers.

shortlist.name: HQ Trust
shortlist.invests: Yes — multi-family office that deliberately backs boutique / specialist managers
shortlist.angle: The Harald-Quandt multi-family office is known for backing boutique and specialist managers — a European FO channel that is genuinely boutique-friendly and USD-capable.
shortlist.access: HQ Trust's manager-selection team (Bad Homburg).
shortlist.watchout: FO-scale tickets; wants clear differentiation.

shortlist.name: FRR & ERAFP (France)
shortlist.invests: Yes — 100% externally managed; award global/Asia equity mandates to external managers via public tender
shortlist.angle: Both French pension funds are entirely externally managed and award global and regional equity mandates by public tender in USD — a clean, structured route for an external manager.
shortlist.access: Their public tender processes (French/EU procurement), usually consultant-supported.
shortlist.watchout: Procurement is formal and ESG-heavy; French-language documentation.

shortlist.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS)
shortlist.invests: Yes — large external programme with a purpose-built emerging-manager / Premier List on-ramp
shortlist.angle: TRS Texas runs one of the most developed emerging-manager programmes in the US, explicitly designed to on-ramp newer external managers, with real appetite for non-US and Asia diversification.
shortlist.access: TRS's Emerging Manager Program / Premier List, usually via its EM-of-EM partners and consultants.
shortlist.watchout: US-time-zone servicing expected; the EM program still has minimums and pacing.

shortlist.name: New York State Common / NYC Retirement Systems
shortlist.invests: Yes — formal emerging-manager and external-equity programmes
shortlist.angle: Both New York systems run established emerging-manager and external-equity programmes and actively seek diversification, including non-US strategies, through external managers.
shortlist.access: Their emerging-manager programmes and public-markets consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Political/governance process; consultant-gated; US-centric operational expectations.

shortlist.name: Illinois Teachers' Retirement System (TRS)
shortlist.invests: Yes — external managers with an active emerging-manager programme
shortlist.angle: A mid-large US pension with a genuine emerging-manager programme and a track record of allocating to external and diverse managers, more approachable than the mega-endowments.
shortlist.access: Illinois TRS emerging-manager programme / consultants.
shortlist.watchout: Consultant-gated; US-servicing expectations.

shortlist.name: Blackstone — BAAM (Strategic Alliance / seeding)
shortlist.invests: Yes — one of the largest hedge-fund allocators and seeders of emerging managers
shortlist.angle: The largest discretionary hedge-fund allocator and a marquee seeder; a BAAM anchor is both large day-one USD capital and a credibility stamp that unlocks other LPs.
shortlist.access: BAAM's seeding / Strategic Alliance and manager-selection teams.
shortlist.watchout: Highly selective; seed capital comes with revenue-share economics.

shortlist.name: Albourne Partners
shortlist.invests: No (advisory) — but rates hedge funds for a vast institutional client base that follows its coverage
shortlist.angle: Albourne is the dominant hedge-fund consultant; being taken under coverage and well-rated effectively unlocks a large pool of institutional LP capital that relies on its ratings — a force-multiplier, not an LP.
shortlist.access: Request coverage from the relevant Albourne strategy analyst.
shortlist.watchout: Not an LP itself; getting rated takes time and full transparency.

shortlist.name: GCM Grosvenor
shortlist.invests: Yes — large allocator to external managers, incl. emerging and diverse managers
shortlist.angle: A large open-architecture allocator with dedicated emerging- and diverse-manager mandates on behalf of institutional clients — a route to multiple underlying LPs through one relationship.
shortlist.access: GCM Grosvenor's manager-research / emerging-manager teams.
shortlist.watchout: Allocates client capital, so gated by their clients' mandates and pacing.

shortlist.name: Investcorp-Tages
shortlist.invests: Yes — dedicated hedge-fund seeding / acceleration platform
shortlist.angle: A dedicated seeding platform whose business is providing day-one anchor capital and acceleration to emerging hedge-fund managers — directly on-thesis for a launch.
shortlist.access: Investcorp-Tages' seeding team.
shortlist.watchout: Seed economics (equity / revenue share) attached; L/S focus.

shortlist.name: Man FRM
shortlist.invests: Yes — hedge-fund solutions / allocator that backs external managers, incl. early-stage
shortlist.angle: A large hedge-fund solutions business that allocates to and incubates external managers globally, with the scale to write meaningful early tickets in USD.
shortlist.access: Man FRM's manager-research / early-stage teams (London / Asia).
shortlist.watchout: Institutional DD; may seek capacity or fee concessions early.

shortlist.name: NewAlpha Asset Management
shortlist.invests: Yes — established emerging-manager seeder / accelerator
shortlist.angle: A specialist emerging-manager seeder that has backed dozens of launches; a natural early conversation for anchor capital in USD.
shortlist.access: NewAlpha's origination team (Paris).
shortlist.watchout: Seed economics; selective on strategy capacity.

shortlist.name: Aksia
shortlist.invests: No (advisory) — advises institutions on hedge-fund and alternatives allocations
shortlist.angle: A leading alternatives consultant whose recommendation gates hedge-fund allocations for many US and global institutions — another access multiplier rather than a direct LP.
shortlist.access: Aksia's hedge-fund research analysts.
shortlist.watchout: Advisory gatekeeper; earning a recommendation requires deep DD.

shortlist.name: UBS Global Wealth Management
shortlist.invests: Yes — aggregates HNW / family-office capital onto its fund platform; large Asia presence
shortlist.angle: The world's largest wealth manager can aggregate substantial HNW and family-office USD capital into a single fund via its platform, and its Asian clients actively seek Asia strategies.
shortlist.access: UBS GWM's hedge-fund / alternatives fund-selection and Asia teams (Hong Kong / Singapore).
shortlist.watchout: Rigorous platform onboarding; suitability and capacity requirements for client money.
